newsitem.title: UK: London precious metals recover off lows.
newsitem.headline: London precious metals recover off lows.

text.p: Gold withstood a test of nearby support on Wednesday afternoon and staged a brisk bounce after fixing at the lowest in more than a month.
The white metals were similarly off their lows after initially testing the downside.
Gold fixed at $346.05 an ounce in the afternoon, the lowest fixing since Febraury 20, compared to $346.80 in the morning.
Prices dipped to the $346 support area under general selling, but then recovered to head back towards $350 after the fixing.
In New York, June gold was up $1.00 at $351.50. Activity focussed on spreads as positions were rolled over to June.
Trading volumes were unexceptional ahead of the long Easter weekend, dealers said, and prices may be content to remain within recent ranges for the time being.
"But gold has done very well to stay above the $346 support after being subjected to the selling we've seen today," a dealer said. "If it's going to move $2-$3, it's going to be up.
Silver was indicated four cents firmer at $5.16/$5.18, lifted by shortcovering, after testing and bouncing up from the $5.10 support level.
Platinum was up $0.50 at $373.00/$374.00 after fixing at $372.00 in the morning, the lowest level since February 21.
Palladium was up even more from Tuesday's weak close, and was last indicated $145.50/$146.50, up $3.25.
The rare white metals had dropped sharply on Tuesday following news that strikes at Russian producer Norilsk were being postponed.
